headline_marked: Bangladesh [[rise to record sixth]] in ICC Test rankings
headline: Bangladesh rise to record sixth in ICC Test rankings
summary: The Tigers climb three places to reach their highest-ever position in Test history, moving ahead of Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
details: Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings, despite a series-ending defeat to Australia in Mackay.
The Tigers now hold 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.
This marks a significant milestone as their previous best ranking was seventh, achieved in May this year following a series victory over Pakistan.
The rise is attributed to a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin during the tour of Australia, which boosted their standing despite the final match loss.
Bangladesh has now moved ahead of several teams including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, the West Indies, and Zimbabwe.
In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a points percentage of 55.56%.
The team currently sits narrowly ahead of India in the WTC standings, having won three of their six matches in the current cycle.
The Tigers will look to strengthen their position as they prepare for an upcoming two-Test series in South Africa.
caption:
A historic milestone for the Tigers! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh has reached its highest-ever ICC Test ranking.

Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings, despite a series-ending defeat to Australia in Mackay.

The Tigers now hold 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.

This marks a significant milestone as their previous best ranking was seventh, achieved in May this year following a series victory over Pakistan.

The rise is attributed to a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin during the tour of Australia, which boosted their standing despite the final match loss.

Bangladesh has now moved ahead of several teams including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, the West Indies, and Zimbabwe.

In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a points percentage of 55.56%.

The team currently sits narrowly ahead of India in the WTC standings, having won three of their six matches in the current cycle.

The Tigers will look to strengthen their position as they prepare for an upcoming two-Test series in South Africa.

headline_marked: 4 killed in Rangpur: [[Family of 4 murdered]] after stopping suspects from taking yaba
headline: 4 killed in Rangpur: Family of 4 murdered after stopping suspects from taking yaba
summary: A retired schoolteacher, his wife, and their two children were killed in their home after the father questioned two men using drugs on the rooftop.
details: A retired schoolteacher, his wife, and their two children were killed in their home in the Daspara area of Rangpur city. Police have detained two cousins in connection with the brutal killings.
The incident began on Thursday night when the two suspects entered the rooftop of Ganapati Chakraborty's house from a neighboring building to consume yaba.
Ganapati, 65, a retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher, went to the roof and questioned the men. To hide their identities, the suspects strangled him with a towel he was carrying.
Hearing the commotion, Ganapati's wife, Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, went upstairs and was strangled by the suspects on the staircase.
The couple's daughter, Agami Chakraborty Prarthi, 23, and son, Priyam Chakraborty, 12, were also killed during the attack.
The bodies were recovered from the locked house on Friday night. Ganapati was found on the roof, Pritilata and Agami on the staircase, and Priyam under a bed.
Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud stated that the suspects were identified through a joint investigation by the RMP, CID, and Detective Branch.
Police noted that the family had no known disputes or enmity with anyone prior to this incident.
caption:
A retired teacher and his entire family were murdered simply for questioning two drug users on their rooftop.

A retired schoolteacher, his wife, and their two children were killed in their home in the Daspara area of Rangpur city. Police have detained two cousins in connection with the brutal killings.

The incident began on Thursday night when the two suspects entered the rooftop of Ganapati Chakraborty's house from a neighboring building to consume yaba.

Ganapati, 65, a retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher, went to the roof and questioned the men. To hide their identities, the suspects strangled him with a towel he was carrying.

Hearing the commotion, Ganapati's wife, Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, went upstairs and was strangled by the suspects on the staircase.

The couple's daughter, Agami Chakraborty Prarthi, 23, and son, Priyam Chakraborty, 12, were also killed during the attack.

The bodies were recovered from the locked house on Friday night. Ganapati was found on the roof, Pritilata and Agami on the staircase, and Priyam under a bed.

Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud stated that the suspects were identified through a joint investigation by the RMP, CID, and Detective Branch.

Police noted that the family had no known disputes or enmity with anyone prior to this incident.
